free_tier.stated: no free tier. The vendor pricing page lists on-demand rates per GPU-hour: H100 SXM (8 GPUs, 80 GB) USD 2.45; A100 SXM (8 GPUs, 80 GB) USD 1.45; A100 SXM (8 GPUs, 40 GB) USD 1.15; A100 PCIe (4 GPUs, 40 GB) USD 1.15; A100 MIG (1 GPU, 20 GB) USD 0.58; A40 (4 GPUs, 48 GB) USD 0.65; GH200 (1 GPU, 96 GB) USD 3.87; Intel Gaudi 2 (8 GPUs, 96 GB) USD 1.10; H200 SXM reserved only. The page lists no L40S, no L4 and no GeForce RTX card. 'Per-Minute Billing': on-demand instances are billed by the minute.

chaining: The Gaudi 2 row at USD 1.10 per GPU-hour with 96 GB of accelerator memory is the cheapest large-memory device and the only non-NVIDIA entry besides Sesterce's AMD lines, so it is the row that matters if the workload can use a non-CUDA toolchain. 30 TB of local storage on that node also makes it a candidate for a job that reads a large corpus once
limits_note: No quota is stated on the vendor pricing page: it publishes price per GPU, GPU count, VRAM, vCPUs, memory, local storage and interconnect. Instances come in 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs on bare metal or virtualized; the A100 MIG row is a single 20 GB slice at USD 0.58 an hour. Reserved contracts save up to 20 percent.
binding_note: No quota is stated on the page: it publishes price, VRAM, host specs, region and status. The wall is the node shape, because the cheapest rate is a four-card node at USD 2.60 an hour total.
